Path 3, fleetGOALS §5.1B

Global Accelerator, Route 53, k8gb

Three ways to move traffic off a dead region, and only one keeps DNS out of the RTO.

WHAT IT IS

Global Accelerator: anycast IPs with failover at the AWS edge. Route 53: health-checked failover and latency records. k8gb: CNCF Incubating, Kubernetes-native global load balancing via CRDs.

WHAT SETS IT APART

Global Accelerator doesn't change DNS, so client caching can't extend recovery, but it's AWS-only. Route 53 and k8gb are both DNS, so TTL is a floor. k8gb is the vendor-neutral one that also covers on-prem.

WHERE WE STAND

Recommend Global Accelerator at the public edge with Route 53 behind it. ⚠️ Get the real failover time and the cost from AWS first.

"k8gb Is Growing Up"; "Building Resilient DNS Infrastructure at Scale", KubeCon NA 2026

DECIDE

Global Accelerator, Route 53, k8gb: Three ways to move traffic off a dead region, and only one keeps DNS out of the RTO. Where we stand: Recommend Global Accelerator at the public edge with Route 53 behind it. ⚠️ Get the real failover time and the cost from AWS first. Decision 2a. What settles it is whether on-prem needs the same mechanism.
